subject: Post-call: model fit evidence + recommended next steps
messages:
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Park <olivia@acme-digital.com>, ml-team@acme-digital.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: model fit evidence + recommended next steps

Hi Olivia / Acme ML team,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — appreciate you walking through the short-context retrieval flow and the throughput targets you shared (goal: 800–1,200 TPS steady-state, p95 latency < 200ms). Per our call, attached and linked below are the Redwood-verified performance snapshots and a compact prompt pack you can use for local regression tests. High-level recap and recommended next steps: 

1) Recommended models for initial pilot (tradeoffs summarized):
   - redwood/gptx-7b-fp16 (balanced): verified for your token mix — household numbers: 980 TPS (batch=16), p50=34ms, p95=170ms, p99=320ms. Good latency headroom and high quality on retrieval-augmented prompts.
   - redwood/rw-3b-q5_0 (cost-optimized): verified throughput 1,500 TPS (batch=32) in our reserved pool, p50=46ms, p95=220ms; slightly softer on few-shot extractive tasks (we include prompt tuning examples).
   - redwood/rw-13b-int8 (quality-first): verified at 420 TPS (batch=8), p50=28ms, p95=130ms, best NLU quality for complex follow-ups. Suggest for higher-value queries or fallback path.

2) What we attached/shared:
   - acme_prompt_set_v1.json (compact prompt set we used in the snapshots)
   - acme_perf_snapshot.csv (per-model TPS/latency rows, environment/seq-length breakdown)
   - redwood_profile_acme_20260922.pdf (concise Redwood-verified profile with test harness notes)
   - Console perf link: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/ACME-2026-045

3) Proposal for immediate pilot (2-week scope):
   - Phase A (days 0–3): run your canonical prompt_set_v1 against gptx-7b-fp16 and rw-3b-q5_0 with the attached prompts; we’ll share an isolation-runbook and a trace collector.
   - Phase B (days 4–10): pilot traffic ramp (10–50% of a shard) with live TTL caching enabled (prefix cache) and Redwood autoscaler configured to your target TPS.
   - Phase C (days 11–14): quality check (regression guardrails) + decision gate (go/no-go recommendations).

4) Notable quality/regression concerns we noticed during qualification:
   - rw-3b-q5_0: occasional entity hallucination on nested-reference prompts; see prompt example #7 in acme_prompt_set_v1.json. We recommend a small post-filter or a reranker.
   - gptx-7b-fp16: very stable, but slightly higher token cost; good baseline for latency-sensitive paths.

Next steps / asks:
   - Can you confirm which model variant you prefer we pilot first (gptx-7b-fp16 or rw-3b-q5_0)?
   - Share a small, redacted sample of your production queries (5–10) if possible — we’ll run them and upload per-query traces.
   - Preferred SLA window and target pilot shard size (approx TPS) so we can pre-configure Dedicated pool limits.

I’ll loop Ben on the infra/runbook side and Grace on rollout/quality checks. Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up to align pilot runbook.

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
jasmine_liu@redwood.ai

From: Olivia Park <olivia@acme-digital.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine_liu@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 22 Sep 2026 18:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: model fit evidence + recommended next steps

Thanks, Jasmine — useful pack. Quick clarifications: 

- Our short-context retrieval workload is mostly single-turn (avg tokens per request ~ 120, response tokens ~40). Peak TPS target is 1,000 for read-heavy paths.
- We prefer to start with the lower-cost profile (rw-3b-q5_0) to validate economics, but we need p95 < 250ms in production. If that looks marginal, we can switch critical traffic to gptx-7b-fp16.

I’ve attached a redacted sample query file (sample_queries_redacted.json) — I’ll upload it to the Drive link you shared.

Can your team run the sample with caching off and then with prefix cache enabled so we can see delta? Also please include the small prompt pack for edge-case #7 that you mentioned.

Olivia
Olivia Park
Staff ML Engineer — ACME Digital

Subject: Redwood perf snapshots + pilot knobs for ACME (note: run instructions inside)

Hi Olivia — forwarding a compact runbook and the performance CSV you asked for. Key notes inline: 

- Cache-off baseline (seq len: 160 / 40): rw-3b-q5_0 = 1,540 TPS (batch=32) p50=52ms p95=235ms p99=410ms in our reserved test environment.
- Prefix-cache enabled (warm KV cache): effective observed TPS jumps to ~2,100 TPS with tail latency improvements: p95 drops to 145ms. This matches the caching delta we discussed; we included a short trace set in acme_perf_snapshot.csv.
- gptx-7b-fp16 baseline: 980 TPS (batch=16) p50=34ms p95=170ms p99=290ms. Higher per-token cost but more headroom for strict latency SLOs.

Pilot knobs I’m provisioning for you if you confirm:
- Dedicated pool shard with autoscaler min=1 / max=6 nodes (GPU type: A750 equivalent).
- Batching policy: max_batch=32, max_latency_ms=40 (start conservative).
- Cache: prefix_kv enabled for read-heavy keys, retention=60s for pilot.

Links (attachments and console):
- Console perf: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/ACME-2026-045
- Runbook (short): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1abcdefgExample

I’ve attached acme_perf_snapshot.csv and redwood_profile_acme_20260922.pdf to this thread. If you want, we can schedule a 30-min tech sync tomorrow morning to run the sample queries live and capture traces.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
